review_output: {"summary":"I found no BLOCKER in this scoped storage and read snapshot. Tenant scoping is correct: queries use the full vendorId, liveId and versionId, the reader re-checks the lease inside the RepeatableRead transaction, and API roles have their access revoked. Rows can't be updated, and they're only deleted when the parent is deleted. Covered rows can't be dated in the future, can't come from before collection started, and are bound to the current revision. Gap rows stay valid across revisions. The open items are prerequisites for activation, not defects in a live path. No trusted producer exists yet, so nothing here proves coverage is real. auditDigest only records provenance.","findings":[{"severity":"MAJOR","issue":"A newly inserted audit row can miss marking a report stale if the audit transaction runs for a long time.","evidence":"The wp20_metric_coverage_changed UPDATE runs under read committed and only sees report rows that are already committed. It takes FOR SHARE on the version row, which does not conflict with other FOR SHARE locks or with plain report inserts. Possible sequence: the audit trigger runs, then a report is created and claimed, then the worker snapshot starts, then the audit commits. The report is never marked stale and its snapshot cannot see the audit.","file":"prisma/migrations/20261015120000_live_metric_coverage_audit/migration.sql","area":"invalidation concurrency","required_test":"Use two connections. Start the audit insert, create and claim a report in the overlapping window, start the snapshot, commit the audit, then try to complete the report. Completion must be rejected.","confidence":0.55,"impact":"A report could be completed on audit state that is already out of date. Severity depends on whether report creation or claiming locks the version row more strongly.","recommended_fix":"Make audit inserts and report creation or claiming contend on the same lock (FOR NO KEY UPDATE on the version row, or an advisory lock). Alternatively, have each audit insert bump a per-version evidence sequence that claim and completion compare."},{"severity":"MAJOR","issue":"A covered row stays valid across a collection outage unless turning collection off or on changes sourceRevision.","evidence":"The guard checks only collectionStartedAt and sourceRevision. It doesn't check collectionEnabled. The reader filters covered rows by sourceRevision alone.","file":"prisma/migrations/20261015120000_live_metric_coverage_audit/migration.sql","area":"certificate validity","required_test":"Insert a covered row, disable collection, then re-enable it or reset collectionStartedAt. The old covered row must no longer count toward complete.","confidence":0.6,"impact":"Once a producer exists, a disabled period could be reported as complete coverage.","recommended_fix":"Before activation, make collectionEnabled and collectionStartedAt structural fields that bump sourceRevision, or write a gap row when collection is disabled. Also reject covered inserts while collection is disabled."},{"severity":"MAJOR","issue":"Coverage is checked only for visits. Registrations and viewing data enter the snapshot without any coverage gate.","evidence":"loadMetricViewingSnapshot calls only readMetricCoverage(tx, lease, 'visits'). Registrations and sessions carry no MetricCoverage, and deliveryComplete is about delivery, not intake coverage.","file":"src/lib/live-metric-report-snapshot.ts","area":"integration prerequisite","required_test":"With full visits coverage and no registrations or viewing audit, any calculated registration or viewing metric must be unavailable, not zero or complete.","confidence":0.7,"impact":"Denominators or viewing metrics from unaudited intake could be shown as complete.","recommended_fix":"Load registrations and viewing coverage in the same snapshot and require complete coverage for every kind the metric uses before the calculator runs."},{"severity":"MINOR","issue":"An audit row doesn't record which producer wrote it, which method or version it used, or which reconciliation run it came from. There is also no idempotency key.","evidence":"The only provenance is auditDigest CHAR(64). There is no producer or run ID column and no unique constraint, so retries create duplicate rows. Each duplicate also invalidates reports again.","file":"prisma/migrations/20261015120000_live_metric_coverage_audit/migration.sql","area":"provenance","required_test":"Insert the same reconciliation twice. It should be a no-op or be rejected, and the row should be traceable to its producer run.","confidence":0.6,"impact":"Rows can't be attributed to a producer or audited later, and retries amplify report invalidation.","recommended_fix":"Add producerId, methodVersion and runId columns, plus a unique key on (scope, kind, runId). Specify how the digest input is canonicalized."},{"severity":"MINOR","issue":"Finely split audit ranges can push a report past the 10,000-row limit and make it permanently unavailable.","evidence":"The reader uses LIMIT 10001 and returns limit_exceeded. Nothing merges adjacent ranges.","file":"src/lib/live-metric-coverage-reader.ts","area":"availability","required_test":"Insert more than 10,000 small covered ranges within one window. The result is limit_exceeded, and producer coalescing should prevent this.","confidence":0.5,"impact":"Reports fail safe but never complete, so this is a liveness problem, not a correctness one.","recommended_fix":"Require the producer to merge contiguous same-revision ranges, or limit how many audit rows are allowed per window."},{"severity":"NIT","issue":"The comment says gaps=[] means an audited empty loss history, but the reader passes [] whenever any covered row exists.","evidence":"The reader passes gaps: rows.length ? ranges('gap') : null. This is safe only because covered rows themselves certify their ranges.","file":"src/lib/live-metric-coverage-reader.ts","area":"semantics/docs","required_test":"Not required. Add a doc assertion.","confidence":0.6,"impact":"Future adapters could misread the contract.","recommended_fix":"Document that a covered row certifies its own range, including that the range has no losses, and that a missing gap row elsewhere is not a zero-loss certificate."},{"severity":"NIT","issue":"The id column has no format check, and the invalidation trigger marks reports stale across all metric kinds.","evidence":"The id column is unconstrained TEXT. The changed trigger ignores kind.","file":"prisma/migrations/20261015120000_live_metric_coverage_audit/migration.sql","area":"hygiene","required_test":"Not required.","confidence":0.5,"impact":"Small: extra recomputation and inconsistent IDs.","recommended_fix":"Add a CHECK on the id format. Over-invalidating across kinds is acceptable to keep as a safe default."}]}
